classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the sector as a cone net: its radius becomes slant height and its arc becomes base circumference. The ordered subparts then guide finding base radius and perpendicular height using sector proportion and Pythagoras.

spec.description: Sector above centre O with B at the left endpoint and A at the right endpoint. Radius OA is labelled 10 cm; the interior angle is labelled 120°. Ordinary source colours map to black; no shading.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the area of the sector shown. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the radii $OA$ and $OB$ are joined together to form the curved surface of a cone, find, correct to two decimal places:

children.label: i
children.prompt: the slant height of the cone

answer.worked: The sector radius becomes the cone’s slant height, so $\ell=10.00\text{ cm}$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the base radius of the cone

answer.short:
$3.33\text{ cm}$

The sector arc becomes the cone’s base circumference.
answer.worked:
The sector arc becomes the cone’s base circumference.
$$\begin{align*}2\pi r&=\frac{120}{360}\times2\pi\times10\\r&=\frac{10}{3}\text{ cm}\\r&\approx3.33\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$9.43\text{ cm}$

Use Pythagoras with slant height $10\text{ cm}$ and exact base radius $\frac{10}{3}\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem, using the exact base radius:
$$\begin{align*}h^2+\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)^2&=10^2\\h^2&=\frac{800}{9}\\h&=\frac{20\sqrt{2}}{3}\text{ cm}\\h&\approx9.43\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
